one_liner: Header-only C++ drop-in std::sort replacement: pattern-defeating quicksort with branchless partitioning and a guaranteed O(n log n) worst case.
what_it_does: pdqsort.h implements pattern-defeating quicksort, a hybrid of quicksort, insertion sort, and heapsort that detects common input shapes (already sorted/reverse-sorted, many equal keys, or ascending-plus-one-out-of-place-element) and sorts them in linear time instead of n log n. It exposes template functions pdqsort(begin, end[, comp]) with the exact calling convention of std::sort, so most call sites can swap std::sort for pdqsort directly. A second entry point, pdqsort_branchless(begin, end[, comp]), forces a branch-free partitioning path; pdqsort itself auto-dispatches to it under C++11 when sorting an arithmetic type with the default std::less/std::greater.
how_it_is_fast: Quicksort with median-of-3 pivoting (Tukey's ninther above 128 elements), switching to insertion sort below 24 elements, and falling back to std::make_heap/std::sort_heap after O(log n) highly unbalanced (<12.5% or >87.5%) partitions, which bounds the worst case at O(n log n) like introsort. After every partition it checks whether the sequence was already partitioned and, if so, attempts a move-bounded insertion sort, giving linear time on sorted/equal/nearly-sorted patterns. For arithmetic types with a default comparator it uses the branchless partitioning technique from Edelkamp & Weiss's BlockQuicksort paper, filling small index buffers with unconditional stores to avoid branch mispredictions during partitioning.
when_to_use: Sorting std::vector/array of built-in arithmetic types (int, float, double) with the default comparator, where the branchless fast path auto-activates
Data likely to contain patterns: nearly-sorted, reverse-sorted, many duplicate keys, or one misplaced element in an otherwise sorted run
Header-only C++03/C++11 codebases that want a drop-in std::sort replacement without adding a build/link dependency
Large arrays (1000+ elements) where branch-misprediction overhead in a naive quicksort partition loop matters
Need a guaranteed O(n log n) worst case (heapsort fallback) without giving up quicksort's average-case speed
when_not_to_use: Need a stable sort (equal elements keep relative order) — no stable variant is provided, unlike std::stable_sort

Comparator itself is expensive (e.g. calls into an interpreted-language callback) — issue #20 shows pdqsort can invoke the comparator more often than glibc qsort/introsort, making it slower than std::sort or qsort when comparison cost dominates
Data shaped like a 'pipe organ' (ascending then descending) sorted against libstdc++ std::stable_sort — the verified README chart shows pdqsort ~2.3x slower there, and roughly tied on 'push front'
Need MSVC 64-bit builds warning-clean — open issue #22 (int64->int conversion warnings) is unresolved
Need std::execution parallel policies or a maintained upstream — no commits since 2021-03-14 and issue #16 (C++17 parallel execution) is still open

integration.dependencies: none (standard library only: <algorithm>, <cstddef>, <functional>, <utility>, <iterator>, plus <cstdint>/<type_traits> under C++11)
integration.min_toolchain: C++03 compiles (branch-based path only); C++11+ enables automatic branchless dispatch and move semantics
integration.platforms: any (portable C++, no SIMD/architecture-specific intrinsics); MSVC 64-bit builds emit C4244 int64->int conversion warnings (open issue #22)
integration.thread_safety: not documented — stateless free template functions with no shared/global state; ordinary iterator-range algorithm semantics apply
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — matches std::sort's call signature exactly (pdqsort(begin, end[, comp])), but it is unstable, so it is a drop-in only for std::sort, not for std::stable_sort

gotchas: Branchless auto-dispatch only triggers for arithmetic value types compared with std::less/std::greater under C++11; custom structs or comparators always take the slower branch-based path unless you call pdqsort_branchless explicitly
Can make more comparator calls than a plain qsort/introsort in some cases (issue #20), so it loses to std::sort/qsort when the comparator itself is costly, even though it does fewer swaps
Switches to std::make_heap/std::sort_heap after O(log n) highly unbalanced partitions, so pathological inputs degrade to heapsort speed, not quicksort speed
Comparator ordering requirements (strict weak ordering vs. total order) are not documented in the README (issue #28, open question, unanswered as of last commit)
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Prefer pdqsort over Highway (vqsort) when you can't require AVX2/AVX3 hardware or want to avoid a SIMD library dependency, and over ska_sort when your keys aren't specifically skewed/geometric-distributed integers. vergesort is the closest comparison (same libstdc++ pattern-detection premise, also unstable-vs-stable tradeoffs), but pdqsort additionally documents a branchless partitioning fast path for arithmetic types with default comparators.
verified_claims_summary: Per the record's verified README bar chart (std::vector<int>, 10^6 elements, i5-4670k @ 3.4GHz, g++ -std=c++11 -O2 -m64 -march=native), pdqsort beat GCC libstdc++ std::sort on all 8 tested distributions, from ~1.9x on shuffled ints to over 10x on ascending/all-equal/push-middle patterns. Against std::stable_sort it was faster on most patterns (~2.4x on shuffled) but ~2.3x slower on pipe organ and about tied on push front.
status_note: Abandoned: no commits since 2021-03-14, the same day an integer-overflow fix (issue #13) landed; a later MSVC-warning issue (#22, 2022) and a C++17 parallel-execution request (#16, 2024) remain open and unaddressed. zlib-licensed and a single ~350-line header, so it's cheap to vendor and patch yourself if needed.
